tasks.short: Visualise historical and future climate change

steps.what: Obtain and verify climate layers and their scientific metadata
Choose comparisons, reference periods, projections and uncertainty representation
Repeat specified GIS selections, layer operations and figure exports
Check scientific meaning, uncertainty and geographic correspondence of all figures
Add checked captions and provenance and save the figure package

tasks.design: First test a saved processing model in the geographic information system represented by {OTHER}; repeat only scientist-specified layer operations and exports. Carry its manifest into a {DOCS} output template, retaining scientific comparison choices, full figure interpretation and the author's ordinary package save.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated layer operations and output formatting can be manual even when calculations already run in software.
tasks.enabler_now: Saved GIS processing models and parameterised figure templates, without a model making climate claims.
tasks.still_hard: Comparability between reconstructed and simulated climates, spatial resolution and honest uncertainty communication.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a visually convincing map implies a comparison the source data cannot support.
tasks.altitude: Spend less time repeating layer operations and more on comparability checks; scientific authority stays unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: GIS processing models can replay specified layer operations and exports; compatibility and scientific interpretation remain human checks.

assumptions: The boundary ends with an internally saved scientific figure package, not public publication. Shares are provisional focal-role labour and exclude all existing model and GIS runtime.

Database maintainers produce layers with variable, units, coordinates, calendar, reference period, scenario or proxy method, uncertainty and source identifiers. s1 checks or manually recovers these fields; absent comparability metadata stops the affected comparison.

s2 produces the exact layer selection, transformations, baseline, map extent and uncertainty treatment. s3 follows this specification, not an inferred scientific method. All manual extraction and compatibility repair remain in s1 and s4.

Test native saved models and templates first. s3 represents actual repeated manual interactions only; where they already run unattended, remove that baseline. s5 removes repeated manifest placement only, retaining caption meaning and the same-system save without approval.
No field collection or new paleoclimate measurements are assumed as ready inputs created for free.
unknowns: Layer coordinate, calendar and unit compatibility
How much export interaction is already automated
research_questions: Replay one real comparison and separate manual interaction from existing GIS runtime
Can the exported manifest preserve calendar, baseline and uncertainty without hand repair?

incremental.description: Maintain layer mappings and verify repeatable output after schema changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 25 repeated-interaction points plus 5 times 20%=1 metadata-placement point, less 1.5 upkeep gives 24.5. With incompatible paleoclimate calendars and projections, only 6 points of compatible layer/export interactions and 0.5 of output metadata placement can be reused; all repair and interpretation remain, giving 5 net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Own scientific comparisons and uncertainty representation while replaying repeatable processing.
role.ambitious_version: Use verified processing reuse to examine additional scientifically comparable periods, without assuming their comparability.
